healthcareSystem: Public healthcare is severely underfunded. Private clinics in Antananarivo offer better care but are expensive by local standards. Tourists should rely on private facilities. Medical infrastructure is very limited outside the capital.
qualityNotes: Healthcare quality is poor by international standards. Private clinics in Antananarivo provide the best available care but are limited. Outside the capital, facilities are very basic. Serious conditions require medical evacuation to Reunion Island, South Africa, or France.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies (pharmacie) open 8am-6pm weekdays, 8am-12pm Saturdays. Very limited availability outside Antananarivo and major towns. Duty pharmacies operate after hours on rotation.
pharmacyTips: Bring all essential medications from home. Pharmacy stock is unreliable and many common medications may be unavailable or counterfeit. French-speaking pharmacists in Antananarivo. Verify medication authenticity. Store medications away from heat and humidity.
prescriptionRules: Prescription enforcement is minimal. Many medications can be purchased without prescription. However, availability is the main concern — stock is limited and counterfeit medications are a risk.

restrictedMeds.name: Opioid medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled. Carry documentation and original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Controlled substances. Bring a doctor's letter in French and English.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Illegal. Strict drug laws in Madagascar.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in French and English for all medications. Bring your entire supply from home — do not rely on finding specific medications in Madagascar. Keep medications in original packaging.

travelInsurance.tips: Essential with comprehensive medical evacuation coverage. Evacuation to Reunion Island or South Africa can cost $30,000+. Ensure coverage for remote areas and adventure activities. Some insurers classify Madagascar as high-risk.

required: Yellow Fever (if arriving from a yellow fever endemic country)
vaccinations.notes: Malaria is a serious risk throughout Madagascar — take prophylaxis and use mosquito protection. Plague outbreaks have occurred. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date.

waterNotes: Do not drink tap water anywhere in Madagascar. Always use bottled, boiled, or purified water. Avoid ice in drinks outside international hotels. Bottled water is available in towns but carry water treatment supplies for remote areas.
foodSafetyTips: Eat only freshly cooked, hot food. Avoid raw vegetables and unpeeled fruit. Street food carries risk — stick to busy stalls with high turnover. Rice (vary) is the staple and usually safe when fresh. Be cautious with seafood outside major coastal restaurants.
medicalTourismNote: Madagascar is not a medical tourism destination. Patients requiring specialized care travel to Reunion Island, South Africa, or France.
metaDescription: Health guide for Madagascar: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, bottled water only, and insurance advice.

hospitals.notes: Private clinic with reasonable facilities. French spoken. One of the better options in the capital.

hospitals.name: Polyclinique d'Ilafy

hospitals.name: Centre Hospitalier de Soavinandriana (CENHOSOA)
hospitals.notes: Military hospital open to public. Better equipped than most public hospitals. Emergency services.

hospitals.name: Hopital Be Toamasina
hospitals.notes: Main hospital in the east coast region. Basic facilities. French and Malagasy spoken.

dentalCare.availability: Very limited. A few private dental practices in Antananarivo. Essentially no dental care in rural areas.
dentalCare.costRange: $10-30 for consultation; $15-50 for fillings; $10-30 for extractions
dentalCare.notes: Handle all dental work before traveling to Madagascar. Equipment and sterilization standards may not meet Western norms.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: For dental emergencies in Antananarivo, ask your hotel or embassy for a recommended dentist. Outside the capital, options are extremely limited.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Essentially unavailable. Very few mental health professionals in the country.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are extremely limited in Madagascar. Online therapy platforms are the only realistic option for English-speaking travelers.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Madagascar has virtually no accessibility infrastructure. Roads are poor, buildings lack ramps and elevators, and terrain is challenging throughout the country.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Even major hospitals have very limited accessibility features.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Private vehicles are the only option. Many roads are unpaved and in poor condition.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Madagascar is extremely challenging for travelers with mobility limitations. Discuss needs extensively with tour operators before booking. National parks have rugged trails. Antananarivo is hilly with steep streets.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.testing: Limited testing available at major clinics in Antananarivo.
covidStatus.notes: Madagascar has lifted COVID entry restrictions.

insuranceClaimProcess: Private clinics provide basic receipts. Documentation standards are inconsistent. Request itemized bills. Payment is often required upfront in cash. Keep all documentation for insurance claims. Your insurer may need to coordinate directly with the clinic.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs at private facilities. Public-system rates are lower but facilities are very basic. Cash payment often required. Actual costs vary significantly.

medicalEvacuation.secondaryDestination: Johannesburg, South Africa or Nairobi, Kenya
medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is absolutely essential for Madagascar. Reunion Island has excellent French healthcare and is the nearest advanced medical hub. Evacuation from remote areas may involve light aircraft to Antananarivo first.
